Communicate mathematical concepts and methods effectively to a range of audiences, both orally and in writing.
Analyze the influence of mathematical sciences and their impact of human activity.
Draw on a global perspective and sound scientific evidence to evaluate the role of mathematical sciences in the international science community.

MATH 4993.title: Capstone Project in Statistics
MATH 4993.description: This is a project-based course that provides students an opportunity to integrate and apply their statistical knowledge to analyzing data. Students may make use of the statistical package SAS to conduct their project. For MATH students in their fourth year of study only.
cilos: Examine the key theories, principles and techniques of data analysis.
Apply independent judgment to objective analysis and prediction of quantitative information.
Apply a rigorous analytic and highly numerate approach to analyze and solve both day-to-day and professional problems.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate statistical outcomes effectively to both lay and expert audiences by utilizing appropriate information and communication technology, through the report writing and project presentation.
Apply an appropriate method to analyze and solve both dayͲtoͲday and professional problems using statistical software.
Appraise the application of statistical modeling to a range of problems and persuade and influence others of its precision and value.

MATH 4994.title: Capstone Project in Mathematics and Economics
MATH 4994.description: This is a project-based course that provides students an opportunity to integrate and apply mathematical tools to analyze problems in economics and social science. Specific topics will be chosen by the instructor. For MATH students in their fourth year of study only.
cilos: Appreciate how to use quantitative tools to analyze issues related to various mathematical models in economics and social science, including fair allocation, voting methods, proportional representation and traffic flows.
Recognize the importance of applying rigorous and numerate approach to analyze and solve problem in economics and social science.
Apply mathematical modeling and analytic proofs to describe and explain phenomena in economics and social science.
Communicate the solutions of mathematical models of economics and social science using mathematical terminology through oral presentation and written reports.

MATH 4995.title: Capstone Project for Data Science
MATH 4995.description: This is a project-based course that trains students on applying computational and analytical tools (matrix computation, Fourier and wavelet transform, convex optimization, etc.) to real-world data analysis problems (recommendation system, signal processing, computer vision, etc.). Familiarity with a programming language is preferred, such as R, Matlab, or Python. For BSc in Data Science and Technology students only.
cilos: Formulate the problem to a mathematical problem.
Find proper analytical and computational tool to solve the problem.
Implement and test the algorithm in a programming language.
Present and interpret the results.

MATH 4996.title: Capstone Project in Financial and Actuarial Mathematics
MATH 4996.description: This is a capstone project for all students majoring in Mathematics under the Financial and Actuarial Mathematics track. Students work on an individual/group project on a selected topic in Financial Mathematics or Actuarial Mathematics under the supervision of an instructor. In particular, the students will explore how to apply various mathematical tools and financial/actuarial knowledge learnt in previous courses to solve some real-life problems in finance or actuarial area. For MATH FAM track students in their fourth year of study only.
MATH 4996.prerequisite: MATH 4427 OR MATH 4511 OR MATH 4512 OR MATH 4514
cilos: Identify problems and formulate the problems using suitable mathematical models.
Explore some advanced and modern mathematical skills for research.
Apply various mathematical tools and statistical method to solve the problems.
Communicate and present research ideas effectively.

MATH 4996.title: Capstone Project in Financial and Actuarial Mathematics
MATH 4996.description: This is a capstone project for all students majoring in Mathematics under the Financial and Actuarial Mathematics track. Students work on an individual/group project on a selected topic in Financial Mathematics or Actuarial Mathematics under the supervision of an instructor. In particular, the students will explore how to apply various mathematical tools and financial/actuarial knowledge learnt in previous courses to solve some real-life problems in finance or actuarial area.
MATH 4996.prerequisite: MATH 4427 OR MATH 4511 OR MATH 4512 OR MATH 4514
cilos: Identify problems and formulate the problems using suitable mathematical models.
Explore some advanced and modern mathematical skills for research.
Apply various mathematical tools and statistical method to solve the problems.
Communicate and present research ideas effectively.

MATH 4999.title: Independent Capstone Project
MATH 4999.description: A capstone project conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. A written report is required. Students need to individually seek a faculty mentor's consent prior to enrollment in this course.
cilos: Explain knowledge, principles and use of precise mathematical language in mathematical theories at college level.
Carry out investigative mathematical work with independent judgment.
Apply rigorous, logical, and analytic methods to execute tasks and solve mathematical problems.
Work independently and collaborate effectively in a team.
Communicate effectively, both in oral and written forms, about mathematical knowledge to audience.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress, and develop motivation and skills for lifelong learning.
Recognize the importance of complying with ethics of science and academic integrity.
Show appreciation of mathematical sciences and its interface with human activities.
View issues in mathematical sciences with reference to the practices of the international science community.

MATH 5011.title: Advanced Real Analysis I
MATH 5011.description: Basic topology, continuous function spaces, abstract measure and integration theory, Lp spaces, convexity and inequalities, Hilbert spaces, Banach spaces, Complex measure.
cilos: Recognize fundamental concepts in the measure theory.
Identify and describe major theorems in the measure theory.
Develop analytic logic and rigorous reasonings.

MATH 5030.title: Complex Function Theory
MATH 5030.description: Review of basic properties of analytic functions. Phragmen-Lindelof principle, normal family, Riemann mapping theorem. Weierstrass factorization theorem, Schwarz reflection principle, analytic continuation, harmonic function, entire function, Hadamard factorization theorem, Picard theorem.
cilos: Understand the geometric nature of residue calculus and analytic functions; lectures; homework.
Learn about the Möbius transformations and their geometric properties.
Understand the use of normal families in the proof Riemann mapping theorem; lectures; homework.
Acquire knowledge of Schwarz-Christoffel mappings and their applications to elliptic integrals; lectures; homework/project presentations.
Acquire knowledge of entire functions and their infinite product representations such as the Gamma functions; lectures; homework/project presentations.
Acquire knowledge of elliptic functions, modular functions and Picard’s theorems; lectures; homework/project presentations.

MATH 5111.title: Advanced Algebra I
MATH 5111.description: Advanced theory of groups, linear algebra, rings, modules, and fields, including Galois theory.
cilos: Recognize the types of algebraic structures such as groups, rings, modules and fields. Build a solid foundation of algebra.
Identify various algebraic structures among mathematics in the framework of category theory.
Apply the algebraic methods and ideas learned in this course to other fields such as algebraic geometry and homological algebra.

MATH 5112.title: Advanced Algebra II
MATH 5112.description: Advanced topics in algebra: group representations, associative algebras, commutative algebra, homological algebra, algebraic number theory.
cilos: Review the basics of abstract algebra and the main concepts in representation theory.
Introduce the main general results about representations of associative algebras.
Survey the main results about representations of finite groups.
Study some more advanced and special topics in the representation theory of finite groups.
Introduce the representation theory of quivers, and classify quivers of finite type.

Provide an introduction to: category theory and abelian categories in particular; homological algebra and its applications to categories of representations; & representation theory of finite dimensional algebras.

MATH 5143.title: Introduction to Lie Algebras
MATH 5143.description: Lie algebras. Nilpotent, solvable and semisimple Lie algebras. Universal enveloping algebras and PBW-theorem. Cartan subalgebras. Roots system, Weyl group, and Dynkin diagram. Classification of semisimple Lie algebras. Representations of semisimple algebras. Weyl character formula. Harish-Chandra isomorphism theorem.
cilos: Understand the concepts and basic techniques of Lie algebras and their representations.
Descrition of the root systems of semisimple Lie algebras.
Learn the properties of Weyl groups.
Classify simply Lie algebra by irreducible root systems.
Study Verma modules and irreducible highest weight modules.

MATH 5145.title: Introduction to Lie Groups
MATH 5145.description: This course is an introduction to the structure and representation theory of compact and noncompact reductive Lie groups.  Topics include general properties of Lie groups and Lie algebras, Peter-Weyl Theorems, representations of compact Lie groups, theorems of the highest weight, Harish-Chandra isomorphism, Weyl character formula, the structure theory of noncompact semisimple and reductive Lie groups, classification of simple real Lie algebras, induced representation and Frobenius reciprocity, classical branching theorems.
cilos: Understand the concepts and basic techniques of Lie groups, Lie algebras and their representations.
Understand the structure of Lie subgroups and Lie subalgebras, and real forms of complex Lie algebras.
Learn the fundamental theorems of Lie theory.
Study orthogonality of characters and Peter-Weyl theorems.
Applications to harmonic analysis.

MATH 5230.title: Differential Topology
MATH 5230.description: Manifolds, embedding and immersion, Sard's theorem, transversality, degree, vector fields, Euler number, Euler-Poincare theorem, Morse functions.
cilos: Manifold and tangent bundle.
Transversality theorem.
Intersection number mod 2.
Intersection number.
Euler number and Poincare-Hopf theorem.
Differential form and Stokes' theorem.

MATH 5240.title: Algebraic Topology
MATH 5240.description: Fundamental group, covering space, Van Kampen theorem, (relative) homology, exact sequences of homology, Mayer-Vietoris sequence, excision theorem, Betti numbers and Euler characteristic.
cilos: Fundamental groupoid and higher homotopy groups.
Singular homology theory.
CW-complex.
Singular cohomology theory.
Poincare duality.

MATH 5251.title: Algebraic Geometry I
MATH 5251.description: Projective spaces, algebraic curves, divisors, line bundles, algebraic varieties, coherent sheaves, schemes. Some commumative algebra and homological algebra such as notherian ring, regular ring, valuation ring, kahler differentials.
cilos: Learn the relations between commuatative algebra and affine varieties and affine schemes.
Master the techchniques using algebra to study geometry.
Learn the concepts of schemes and basic properties of schemes.
Learn the sheaves of modules on schemes.

MATH 5261.title: Algebraic Geometry II
MATH 5261.description: Derived functors, cohomology of coherent sheaves on schemes, extension groups of sheaves, higher direct image of sheaves, Serre duality, flat morphisms, smooth morphisms, and semi-continuity, basics of curves and surfaces.
cilos: Deeper understanding of using algebra to study geometry.
Learn the key geometry concepts of schemes using algebraic methods.
Master the viewpoint of Grothendieck's cohomology formulation.
Study various cohomology of coherent sheaves.

MATH 5270.title: Mathematical Structures in Modern Statistical Physics and Quantum Field Theory
MATH 5270.description: Over the past decades, contemporary theoretical physics has substantially influenced the development of numerous novel mathematical theories which became central subjects of current research in mathematics. This course focuses on some of these mathematical theories coming from subjects including Statistical Physics (SP), Quantum Field theory (QFT), and Gravity (Gr). This course aims at introducing advanced mathematical concepts which are pivotal in the rigorous study of various models in SP, QFT and Gr, using basic tools from probability and geometry.
cilos: Understand the various mathematical approaches to models in statistical physics and quantum (field) theory, including the constructions of path integrals
Apply probabilistic, analytic, combinatorics and representation methods to study problems in mathematical physics
Understand approaches to problems in physics from geometry and statistical physics
Understand aspects of the discrete and continuum Gaussian Free Field (GFF) and its geometry

MATH 5281.title: Partial Differential Equations
MATH 5281.description: This is an introductory postgraduate course on Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). We will start with the classical prototype linear PDEs, and introduce a variety of tools and methods. Then we will extend our beginning theories to general situation using the notion of Sobolev spaces, Holder space and weak solutions. We will prove the existence, uniqueness, regularity and other properties of weak solutions.
cilos: Recognize the types of second-order PDEs as typified by classical equations of mathematical physics, such as the wave equation, heat equation and Laplace equation.
Identify and describe the major theories of general PDEs.
Apply the tools of calculus, linear algebra and real analysis in a coherent way to PDE problems.
Apply the knowledge of PDEs to physical sciences and engineering, and physically interpret the solutions.
Use different methods, such as Fourier transform, separation variables, characteristics, similarity, power series to solve PDEs.

MATH 5285.title: Applied Analysis
MATH 5285.description: Contraction mapping theorem, Fourier series, Fourier transforms, Basics of Hilbert Space theory, Operator theory in Hilbert Spaces, Basics of Banach space theory, Convex analysis.
cilos: Explain the key ideas and concepts behind various analytical techniques.
Identify situations where analytical techniques are applicable.
Recognize limitations of the analytical techniques.
Develop extension of generalization for the techniques.
Implement the techniques to problems in various situations.

MATH 5311.title: Advanced Numerical Methods I
MATH 5311.description: Numerical solution of differential equations, finite difference method, finite element methods, spectral methods and boundary integral methods.  Basic theory of convergence, stability and error estimates.
cilos: Recognize and use appropriately numerical techniques in computation.
Develop numerical scheme to discretize partial differential equations.
Apply numerical analysis to examine the consistency, stability and convergence of the numerical methods.
Apply appropriate numerical schemes to solve real and hypothetical problems.

MATH 5312.title: Advanced Numerical Methods II
MATH 5312.description: Direct and iterative methods. Programming techniques and softwares libraries. Sparse solvers, Fast algorithms, multi-grid and domain decomposition techniques.
cilos: Understand direct and iterative algorithms for solving linear systems, and their convergence theory.
Identify suitable algorithms to solve linear equations arising from practical science and engineering problems, and implement them on a computing platform.
Understand algorithms and theories of other numerical linear algebra problems including the least squares problem and the eigenvalue problem.

MATH 5350.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics for Inviscid Flows
MATH 5350.description: Derivation of the Navier-Strokes equations; the Euler equations; Lagriangian vs. Eulerian methods of description; nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws; characteristics and Riemann invariants; classification of discontinuity; weak solutions and entropy condition; Riemann problem; CFL condition; Godunov method; artificial dissipation; TVD methods; and random choice method.
cilos: Understand the characteristics in linear and nonlinear scalar equations, the concept of entropy, and the condition for the formation of discontinuous shock. Solve the Riemann problem for the nonlinear scalar equation with concave and convex flux functions. Develop numerical scheme to solve the Burgers’ equation and traffic flow equation.
Identify the characteristic variables for the linear hyperbolic system. Construct the analytical solution of the Riemann problem. Develop numerical scheme to solve the linear system.

Obtain the characteristic variables for the nonlinear 2x2 system, such as the shallow water equations. Construct the analytical similarity solution for the Riemann problem and apply it to the wave interactions.

Derive the gas dynamic Euler equations. Present the Euler equations in terms of conservative, characteristic and primitive variables. Construct the Riemann solution for the Euler equations. Identify the interaction among different kinds of waves.
Develop numerical scheme for the Euler equations. Understand approximate Riemann solvers. Construct reliable numerical schemes beyond the inviscid Euler equations.

MATH 5351.title: Mathematical Methods in Science and Engineering I
MATH 5351.description: Modeling and analytical solution methods of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). Topics include: derivation of conservation laws and constitutive equations, well-posedness, traveling wave solutions, method of characteristics, shocks and rarefaction solutions, weak solutions to hyperbolic equations, hyperbolic Systems, linear stability analysis, weakly nonlinear approximation, similarity methods, calculus of variations.
cilos: Demonstrate abilities to describe problems in science and engineering by partial differential equation models.
Apply analytical solution methods to solve nonlinear partial differential equations.
Apply approximation methods to solve nonlinear partial differential equations.
Demonstrate abilities to interpret the solutions of partial differential equation models for problems in science and engineering.

MATH 5352.title: Mathematical Methods in Science and Engineering II
MATH 5352.description: Asymptotic methods and perturbation theory for obtaining approximate analytical solutions to differential equations. Topics include: local analysis of solutions to differential equations, asymptotic expansion of integrals, global analysis and perturbation methods, WKB theory, multiple-scale analysis, homogenization method.
cilos: Demonstrate abilities to obtain approximate analytical solutions  to differential equations by asymptotic methods.
Identify perturbation problems in science and engineering.
Demonstrate abilities to understand the errors of the obtained approximate analytical solutions.

MATH 5353.title: Multiscale Modeling and Computation for Non-equilibrium Flows
MATH 5353.description: Introduction of the Navier-Strokes equations and the flow modeling in the hydrodynamic scale. The derivation of the Boltzmann equation in the kinetic scale. The basic mathematical analysis of the Chapman-Enskog expansion and the numerical methods for the Boltzmann equation. The multiscale modeling from the kinetic to the hydrodynamic scales and the discretized governing equations. The study of non-equilibrium transport phenomena in gas dynamics, radiative and heat transfer, and plasma physics.
cilos: Derive the Navier-Stokes equations in the hydrodynamic scale.
Model the particle transport and collision and derive the Boltzmann equation in kinetic scale.
Extend the kinetic scale modelling to other scales and construct the corresponding governing equations.
Develop numerical scheme for multiscale transport equations.
Use multiscale method to study transport problems in rarefied gas dynamics, radiative and heat transfer, and plasma simulation.

MATH 5380.title: Combinatorics
MATH 5380.description: Enumerative Combinatorics: bijective counting, permutation statistics, generating functions, partially ordered sets, Mobius inversions, Polya theory.  Graph Theory: cycle space, bond space, spanning-tree formulas, matching theory, chromatic polynomials, network flows.  Matroid Theory: matroid axioms, representations, duality, lattice of flats, transversals.
cilos: Develop a kind philosophy of discrete thinking and bijective counting.
Develop an understanding of the core ideas and concepts of advanced combinatorics.
Recognize the power of abstraction and generalization, and apply logical reasoning to investigate mathematical work with independent judgement.
Apply rigorous, analytic, highly quantitative approach to analyze and solve problems using combinatorial technics.
Understand the uni¯cation of discrete and continuous thought by demonstrating part of taught theories.

MATH 5411.title: Advanced Probability Theory I
MATH 5411.description: Probability spaces and random variables, distribution functions, expectations and moments, independence, convergence concepts, law of large numbers and random series.
cilos: Develop a rigorous mathematical framework to analyze randomness based on measure theory.
Derive probability inequality as a useful tool for mathematical analysis.
Demonstrate various forms of laws of large numbers and large deviation and their applications.
Establish the central limit theorem and present their applications.
Apply random walk theory to actuarial analysis.

MATH 5412.title: Advanced Probability Theory II
MATH 5412.description: Stable laws; infinitely divisible distributions; weak convergence on general metric spaces; Donsker’s invariance principle; basic martingale theory; optional stopping theorem; martingale convergence theorems; martingale CLT; Concentration inequalities; logarithmic Sobolev inequality; large deviation.
cilos: Recognize the basic knowledges about martingale, Brownian motion, and functional limit theorems.
Identify and describe the major theories of martingale CLT and functional CLT.
Apply the martingale approach to establish nonlinear functionals of random variables.
Apply functional limiting theorem  to get the limiting behavior of various statistics for stochastic process.

MATH 5431.title: Advanced Mathematical Statistics I
MATH 5431.description: Theory of statistical inference in estimation. Topics include: sufficiency, ancillary statistics, completeness, UMVU estimators, information inequality, efficiency, asymptotic maximum likelihood theory. Other topics may include Bayes estimation and conditional inference.
cilos: Develop a rigorous mathematical framework and lay a firm foundation for statistical inference.
Recognize the most important concepts, including sufficiency, MLE, efficiency, risk, admissibility.
Employ appropriate statistical models for modeling and inference.
Recognize the different criterion for evaluation of statistical models.
Apply the theory in mathematical statistics to real-life problems.

MATH 5432.title: Advanced Mathematical Statistics II
MATH 5432.description: Theory of statistical inference in hypothesis testing. Topics include: uniformly most powerful tests, unbiasedness, invariance, minimax principle, large-sample parametric significance tests. Concept of decision theory also covered.
cilos: Recognise the problem of interest and formulate the corresponding testing hypotheses.
Identify the types of random mechanisms for the problem at hand, and then choose the appropriate models to describe the data.
Choose the most powerful tests if available and/or the most feasible tests.
Evaluate and compare different types of tests.
Decide whether it is appropriate to use parametric tests or nonparametric tests.
Develop problem-solving skills to handle real-life problems with uncertainty.

MATH 5450.title: Stochastic Processes
MATH 5450.description: Theory of Markov processes, second order stationary theory, Poisson and point processes, Brownian motion, Martingales and queueing theory.
cilos: Introduce the general concept of stochastic process  and Markov chain.
Study the properties of  Markov chain   and  its limiting distributions.
Study the periodic Markov chain and its properties.
Study  martingale convergence theory and option sampling theory.
Study  Brownian motion and its properties.

MATH 5460.title: Time Series Analysis
MATH 5460.description: Basic idea of time series analysis in both the time and frequency domains. Topics include: autocorrelation, partial ACF, Box and Jerkins ARIMA modeling, spectrum and periodogram, order selection, diagnostic and forecasting. Real life examples will be used throughout the course.
cilos: Introduce some basic  concepts in time series   such as auto-covariance, stationarity  and ergodicity.
Introduce  time series models, such as AR models, ARMA models, threshold models, GARCH models,  and study their properties.
Study the theory of  estimation and testing statistics of  time series models.
Study the diagnostic tools for  identifying various models in practice.
Introduce for possible applications such as option theory and risk management.

MATH 5470.title: Statistical Machine Learning
MATH 5470.description: This course covers methodology, major software tools and applications in statistical learning. By introducing principal ideas in statistical learning, the course will help students understand conceptual underpinnings of methods in data mining. The topics include regression, logistic regression, feature selection, model selection, basis expansions and regularization, model assessment and selection; additive models; graphical models, decision trees, boosting; support vector machines; clustering.
cilos: Describe the basic procedures in data analysis.
Explain the principles behind statistical learning tools.
Analyze data with real data.
Draw meaningful implications in decision making.
Write a good project report and help decision making in practice.

MATH 5471.title: Advanced Machine Learning with Graphs
MATH 5471.description: This course will introduce a number of advanced learning methods and modeling principles for analyzing large-scale complex data structures and graph data. Topics covered include semi-supervised learning, spectral graph theory, deep graph modeling, knowledge graph modeling, etc., as well as open research problems in this area.
cilos: Demonstrate machine learning algorithm design skills for graph data analytics tasks.
Analyze the quality of results to domain problems.
Develop a program that can handle existing real problems.

MATH 5472.title: Computer Age Statistical Inference with Applications
MATH 5472.description: This course is designed for RPg students in applied mathematics, statistics, and engineering who are interested in learning from data. It covers advanced topics in statistical learning and inference, with emphasis on the integration of statistical models and algorithms for statistical inference. This course aims to first make connections among classical topics, and then move forward to modern topics, including statistical view of deep learning. Various applications will be discussed, such as computer vision, human genetics, and text mining.
cilos: Describe the basic procedures in data analysis.
Explain the principles behind statistical inference.
Analyze real data.
Draw meaningful implications in decision making.
Write a good report.
Implement algorithms for statistical inference.

MATH 5473.title: Topological and Geometric Data Reduction and Visualization
MATH 5473.description: This course is a mathematical introduction to data analysis and visualization with a perspective of topology and geometry. Topics covered include: classical linear dimensionality reduction, the principal component analysis (PCA) and its dual multidimensional scaling (MDS), as well as extensions to manifold learning, topological data analysis, and sparse models in applied math/high dimensional statistics. Extensive application examples in biology, finance, and information technology are presented along with course projects.
cilos: Explain the basics concept of dimensional reduction.
Use Compressed Sensing and High Dimensional Statistics techniques for data analysis.
Use Manifold learning approach for applications.
Apply the data analysis method in applications.

MATH 5520.title: Interest Rate Models
MATH 5520.description: Theory of interest rates, yield curves, short rates, forward rates.  Short rate models: Vasicek model and Cox-Ingersoll-Ross models.  Term structure models: Hull-White fitting procedure.  Heath-Jarrow-Morton pricing framework.  LIBOR and swap market models, Brace-Gatarek-Musiela approach.  Affine models.
cilos: Explain fixed-income markets and the roles of the fixed-income derivatives.
Apply advanced mathematical tools for fixed-income modeling.
Identify risk factors of fixed-income derivatives and formulate major classes of fixed-income models accordingly.
Evaluate the effectiveness of various models for different sectors of fixed-income derivatives.
Analyze exotic derivatives, identify proper pricing models and strategies for hedging.

MATH 6771.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students basic training in teaching skills, research management, career development in and outside academia, and related professional skills in Mathematics.
